next_step: POC soak test on Dedicated pool + final security questionnaire
notes:
Background: Saffron Bridge runs patient contact centers for three regional hospital systems. Heavy voice+chat mix. Current pain: agents spend 35-50% time context-switching between EHR, CRM and triage scripts. Looking for streaming agent assist that does: real-time suggested replies, summary of prior messages, and tool-calling (open EHR rows, create ticket) via secure connectors.

Key quotes: "If suggestions arrive >200ms it's unusable on phone — need p95 end-to-end under 150ms for suggested snippets", — Director, Contact Center (L. Morales).

Requirements summary: streaming token-level suggestions with mid-conversation updates; partial-token streaming to UI; deterministic guardrails and domain-specific redaction (PHI masking); audit logs per suggestion and per tool-call; ability to pin model version per hospital region; configurable fallback to smaller local quantized model during spikes; retention controls for transcripts (90 days default, opt-in 7 years for audit).

Compliance: must pass vendor SOC2/ISO27001 proofing, support SSO/SAML with SCIM user sync, provide KMS integration for key management, and offer data residency for EU and CA patients.

POC goals: integrate Redwood Dedicated pool with connector to Epic EHR sandbox, demonstrate <150ms avg suggestion latency for chat load of 300 concurrent agents, show audited tool-call replay for 500 actions, quantify per-token cost vs baseline.

Notes / shorthand: POC scope split: week1 infra + security signoff, week2 connector + demo UI, week3 soak & spike tests, week4 cost report + legal review. SE asked for sample kernel/quantization guidance for conversation lengths >1024 tokens. CSM to coordinate compliance doc handoff to legal.
